context_requirements: Expression of functional ATP-sensitive potassium (KATP) channel subunits (ABCC8/SUR1, KCNJ11/Kir6.2, KCNJ8/Kir6.1, KCNJ10/Kir4.1, KCNJ1/Kir1.1)
A cellular context in which KATP channel activity is coupled to transcriptional programs (e.g., excitable cells, insulin-secreting cells, or cells under metabolic/oxidative stress)
Presence of a KATP-channel-dependent transcriptional pathway; most immortalized cancer lines lack this coupling
falsifiers: Reproducible concentration-dependent changes in landmark gene expression at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine cell lines
Shared transcriptional signature across multiple cell lines that is reversed by a KATP channel opener
Enrichment of KATP channel subunit expression correlating with response magnitude across lines

evidence.supports: KATP channel blocker glybenclamide abolishes isoflurane postconditioning in endothelial cells, indicating KATP channels can mediate cellular responses in some contexts
Mitochondrial KATP channel opener iptakalim protects PC12 cells via regulation of bcl-2 and bax, showing KATP channel modulation can affect apoptosis-related gene expression
Mitochondrial KATP channel opener diazoxide triggers cardioprotection against oxidative stress-induced apoptosis in cardiomyocytes
Human hair follicles express KATP channel subunits SUR1, SUR2B, Kir6.1, Kir6.2 and respond to minoxidil and tolbutamide, demonstrating KATP channel expression in non-excitable human cells
